newsitem.title: USA: Members of Congress back Oklahoma bombing victims.
newsitem.headline: Members of Congress back Oklahoma bombing victims.

text.p: Members of Congress prepared Wednesday to support victims of the Oklahoma City bombing who want to attend the upcoming trial of one of the accused bombers and also appear as witnesses; two courts have said they cannot.
The trial of Timothy McVeigh will begin March 31.
A spokesman for Representative Frank Lucas, R-Okla., said at least 28 representatives will file a "friend of the court" brief Friday with the federal appeals court in Denver.
The Justice Department also plans to ask the judges to reconsider the ruling, a Justice Department source said.
Ordinarily, in federal court witnesses are excluded from a trial until they are called to testify in order to avoid being influenced by the previous testimony.
But Oklahoma City bombing victims, who would testify in the penalty phase of the trial in case of a conviction, are seeking an exception.

McVeigh and Terry Nichols are awaiting separate trials for the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building. The explosion claimed 168 lives. No trial date has been set for Nichols.
Last year, the trial judge said victims had to choose between attending court proceedings and testifying.
About 80 people, supported by victims rights groups, appealed. A three-judge panel of the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals last week upheld the trial judge.
On Friday, the victims will ask all 12 judges on the appeals court to reconsider the ruling made by the panel, a victims' attorney said.

Separately, attorneys for McVeigh asked the court to hold a hearing so they can challenge prosecutors' plans to put on the stand at the upcoming trial eyewitnesses whose testimony would track McVeigh's movements prior to the bombing.
